jobs.title: Civil Engineer - Ecosystem Restoration
jobs.description:
As a Civil Engineer with Civil & Environmental Consultants, Inc. (CEC) in our Pittsburgh, PA office, you won’t spend your first years watching from the sidelines. You’ll contribute to real projects from the start, working alongside experienced engineers and scientists to shape the region’s most exciting stream, wetland, and floodplain restoration projects. If you’re looking to develop strong technical skills, learn from people who want to teach, and do work that you can point to, this is the place to launch your career.

As a 100% employee-owned firm, CEC offers a unique opportunity to build long-term wealth while developing your engineering skills and advancing your career. If you're looking for project variety, strong mentorship, and a collaborative environment where you can continue growing professionally, CEC provides the resources and support to help you succeed.

Responsibilites

You will build practical engineering skills including grading, stormwater management, erosion and sediment control, permitting, and hydrologic and hydraulic modeling. You will help to design ecological restoration projects that reconnect streams to floodplains, restore wetlands, improve aquatic habitat, enhance water quality, and create lasting benefits for communities
No two projects are exactly alike. One day you may help transform a degraded stream corridor into a thriving ecosystem; another may involve restoring hundreds of acres of floodplain and wetlands or designing resilient infrastructure for renewable energy projects
Along the way, you'll work closely with Project Managers, clients, contractors, and regulatory agencies, gaining valuable experience and visibility throughout the project lifecycle
Your experience will extend beyond the computer screen. From field investigations and drone-assisted site assessments to conceptual design, regulatory permitting, construction oversight, and ultimately seeing a restored stream flow through a newly created floodplain, you'll see how your work takes shape in the real world

What We Offer

Sign-on bonus for eligible candidates
100% employee-owned firm with access to ownership opportunities beginning within your first year
Competitive compensation with multiple income streams, including performance bonuses and employee ownership
55% of company profits distributed back to employees through bonuses
Flexible and hybrid work schedule options
Comprehensive benefits beginning on day one, including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance
401(k) with company match beginning the first of the month following your start date
Collaborative environment that supports mentorship, technical development, and career growth
Access to on-site amenities including a fitness center, café, recreation areas, and employee events
Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering; Master’s degree is a plus
Previous Internship preferred or 1+ years of professional engineering experience
Engineering in Training (EIT) certification preferred
Familiarity with AutoCAD/Civil 3D, HydroCAD, HEC-RAS, HEC-HMS or Storm Sewers a plus
Attention to detail, strong problem-solving skills, and strong verbal and written communication skills

We have experts! CEC is consistently ranked as a Top 500 Design Firm and Top 200 Environmental Firm by Engineering News-Record
. We are looking for people who enjoy using their education and experience to solve difficult technical problems and work on interesting projects. You can accomplish this while working with a team of professionals who are equally motivated to provide high levels of service to our clients and to teach you along the way.

We have support! We have a variety of Employee Resource Groups, including CEC Community - focused on giving back to the communities in which we work; CEC Ignite - focused on helping professionals early in their careers to develop their pathway; CEC iDEA - focused on inclusion, diversity, equality, and acceptance; and CEC Women - focused on creating internal and external opportunities for women to network and leverage professional experience!

We care about our people! People and Culture are two of the five elements of our strategic plan. When you care about your people, they will want to grow a career with you - that is our goal. CEC offers you a small-firm work environment with large-firm opportunities. Not only will we help you develop professionally, but we will also provide an opportunity to become an owner of the firm and share in its success.

CEC offers a matching 401(k); profit sharing; a performance bonus; company stock; medical, dental, and vision insurance; short and long-term disability; tuition assistance; professional development; and work-life balance.

CEC is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in recruiting, hiring or promotion based on race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, transgender status), national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status or any other basis or characteristic prohibited by applicable federal, state, or local law.

THIRD PARTY RECRUITERS

If CEC has not expressly requested recruiting services or contractually engaged with you for recruiting services on a specific position, any resumes or candidate profiles sent to CEC shall be considered unsolicited. Therefore, any such submissions will be considered property of CEC, with no associated fees due to your firm.

jobs.description:
Job Family Group

HSSE Group

Job Description

About bp / bpx

At bp, we’re reimagining energy for people and our planet. Within Production & Operations, bpx energy plays a critical role in delivering reliable energy while advancing our low carbon ambitions and reducing emissions across our operations.

Role Synopsis

The Environmental Engineer – Low Carbon is the subject matter expert in supporting bpx’s methane and carbon initiatives through emissions forecasting and accounting of emission projects, certification program coordination, and development of clear, data driven narratives. This role contributes to improving data quality and reporting transparency, and assists in air engineer job duties such as preparation of emission inventories and understanding sophisticated air regulations.

Key Responsibilities

Leading greenhouse gas forecasting by applying strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and sound judgment to recurring planning and reporting cycles.
Coordinating methane certification and assurance activities by organizing evidence, preparing for audits, tracking actions, and collaborating with internal teams and external reviewers.
Creating clear, compelling narratives and recommendations that explain methane management and emissions performance.
Determining insights by capturing inputs, performing quality checks, analyzing trends and variances, and maintaining clear documentation.
Partnering across environmental, engineering, operations, and digital teams to define data needs, resolve issues, and translate business requirements into practical, scalable solutions.
Simplify workflows, strengthen data governance, standardize processes, and identify opportunities to reduce manual effort and continuously improve.
Multi-functional and providing support in traditional environmental areas (e.g., air quality compliance, reporting) as business needs require.

Essential Education & Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or related technical field.
8 or more years of environmental, sustainability, or engineering roles with an emphasis on air quality in the oil and gas industry.
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to translate technical information into clear narratives.
Statistical and analytical thinking: Ability to evaluate datasets, perform basic statistical analysis, and identify trends, anomalies, and patterns in emissions or operational data.
Pattern recognition & problem solving: Ability to connect data insights to operational drivers and support development of actionable improvements.
Digital and data collaboration: Ability to work optimally with IT, data, or digital teams to define data needs, troubleshoot issues, and enable delivery of accurate and timely outputs to the business.
Strategic awareness: Interest in understanding how current data, tools, and processes support broader methane and carbon reduction goals, with the ability to contribute to discussions on future-state improvements.
Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill technical information into clear, stakeholder messaging.

Preferred Experience

Exposure to greenhouse gas inventories, emissions data, or sustainability reporting.
Curiosity about methane management, carbon reduction, or energy transition initiatives.

Why Join Us

You’ll be part of a team driving meaningful progress toward methane reduction and lower carbon energy systems—while gaining exposure to both low carbon strategy and traditional environmental engineering disciplines within a collaborative and fast paced environment.

Salary And Benefits

We offer a reward and wellbeing package to enable your work to fit with your life. These can include, but not limited to, access to health, vision and dental insurance, flexible working schedule, paid time off policy, discretionary annual bonus program, long-term incentive program, and a generous 401K matching program. How much do pay (base)? $130,000 - $160,000

Note that the pay range listed for this position is a good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible base compensation at the time of posting.

Travel Requirement

Up to 10% travel should be expected with this role

Relocation Assistance:

This role is not eligible for relocation

Remote Type

This position is a hybrid of office/remote working

Skills

Agility core practices, Agility core practices, Air Quality Management, Biodiversity Management, Carbon intensity measurement, Carbon Management, Chemical hazard management, Communication, Community Engagement, Continuous Learning, Cost-conscious decision-making, Crisis and emergency response management, Data Analysis, Environmental Legal Compliance, Environmental Management, Environment and Social Group Reporting, Environment and Social Impact Assessment, Environment and Social Project Compliance Analysis, HSE data knowledge, HSSE auditing and self-verification, Influencing, Life cycle and circularity, Noise emissions management, OMS and bp requirements, Remediation Management {+ 4 more}

Legal Disclaimer

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, socioeconomic status, neurodiversity/neurocognitive functioning, veteran status or disability status. Individuals with an accessibility need may request an adjustment/accommodation related to bp’s recruiting process (e.g., accessing the job application, completing required assessments, participating in telephone screenings or interviews, etc.). If you would like to request an adjustment/accommodation related to the recruitment process, please contact us.

If you are selected for a position and depending upon your role, your employment may be contingent upon adherence to local policy. This may include pre-placement drug screening, medical review of physical fitness for the role, and background checks.

jobs.title: Sample Receiving Technician, Eurofins Environmental Testing South Central, Little Rock, AR
jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Environment Testing in Little Rock, AR is seeking a Sample Receiving Technician to join our team. Our laboratory specializes in environmental testing. Providing analytical data and support to a diverse range of clients.

The Sample Receiving Technician is responsible for logging and tracking the receipt and shipment of samples into and out of the laboratory, verifying sample receipt, and supporting accurate and timely documentation. This role assists with preparing bottle kits for client delivery, sample login, labeling, routing, prioritization, and storage in accordance with Chain of Custody requirements and documented procedures. The Sample Receiving Technician may also support sample pick-up and delivery, customer service, courier duties, and the proper disposal of samples and waste in accordance with applicable procedures.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Receive and unload incoming samples or consignments in accordance with SOP; verify receipt against the Chain of Custody (COC), match samples to the corresponding quote, and document discrepancies daily. Review COCs for accuracy, completeness, and correctness, and seek resolution when needed.
Log samples into the laboratory information management system daily and assign job numbers for tracking purposes; distribute associated paperwork to Project Managers.
Label samples with assigned job numbers and deliver them to the appropriate laboratories for analysis each day.
Prepare bottle kits daily for shipment to clients for sample collection and return analysis, following established procedures, including EPA and DOT requirements.
Ship samples to other laboratories in accordance with DOT regulations when testing is not performed at the local facility.
Dispose of spent samples, waste, and other potentially hazardous materials in accordance with established procedures.
Clean and organize the department daily to maintain a safe, orderly work environment.
Maintain and promote safety by conducting all operations in a safe and environmentally compliant manner.
Stock supplies and assist with inventory management to ensure appropriate quantities of materials are available to perform assigned tasks.
Perform sample splitting and composites as requested.
Perform courier duties as needed to support laboratory and client requirements.
Comply with all driver procedures, certification requirements, and company driver policies.
Organize walk-in coolers to support sample storage and retrieval.
Ship empty coolers back to clients and other Eurofins laboratories; log all outgoing coolers to maintain a detailed cooler inventory.
Conduct all client interactions in a professional and courteous manner.
Perform other duties as assigned by local management.

Qualifications

High school diploma or GED required.
Valid state-issued driver’s license to operate company vehicles.
Basic computer skills include; ability to accurately input data into LIMS systems and ability to manage multiple emails.
Must be able to lift 55 lbs routinely and safely and must be able to work standing for most of the day
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English

Additional Information

This is a full time position Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. Some weekend work and overtime may be required.

Pay Rate Range for this position is $17 -$21 / hour (DOE).

Candidates within a commutable distance to Little Rock, AR are encouraged to apply.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

jobs.description:
Company Description

This is a Position-Based Test conducted in accordance with CSC Rule 111A.

Application Opening Date: September 28, 2026
Application Filing Deadline: October 16, 2026 at 11:59PM (PDT)
Location: 1 Lakeshore Drive, Moccasin, CA, Moccasin, California, United States
Recruitment ID: PBT-5298-167779/ RTF0167778

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Natural Resources and Lands Management Division:

The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on SFPUC lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations.

About the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section of NRLM:

The Moccasin Planning and Compliance (MPC) team is responsible for environmental review and permitting for the eastern division of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System and Hetch Hetchy Water and Power (HHWP), an operating division operating water, wastewater, and power infrastructure across the Sierra Nevada to the Bay Area.

Working Relationships:

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams.

The position requires effective communication, sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to develop productive working relationships with individuals who may have different technical expertise, responsibilities, priorities, or perspectives.

Role Location:

There is currently one position available with the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division of the Water Enterprise. The position is located in Moccasin, California and the reporting location is in Moccasin, CA
(located 140 miles east of the San Francisco Bay Area
, requiring a 5-hour round trip commute from the San Francisco Bay Area, by car in fair weather).

Working Location:

The nature of the work may require working in remote field settings, including watersheds, streams, rivers, reservoirs, and federal lands. Duties may require driving or hiking to remote locations using unimproved dirt or mountain roads and working outdoors in inclement weather.

Job Description

Role Description:

The Environmental Planner performs complex environmental planning, permitting, compliance, and lands management work supporting operational and Capital Improvement Program activities of the SFPUC Water Enterprise, including CEQA/NEPA environmental review, Chapter 31 implementation, resource-agency permitting, environmental construction compliance, professional-services administration, federal-land coordination, natural and cultural resources management, Tribal engagement, and strategic program development.

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams. The incumbent develops project descriptions; evaluates environmental impacts and mitigation measures; prepares, manages, and reviews technical studies and regulatory documentation; supports professional services contract administration; coordinates multidisciplinary project teams; and provides technical guidance regarding environmental review, permitting, and regulatory compliance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Analyzes proposed project activities to determine environmental review, documentation, consultation, and permitting requirements, identifies environmental and regulatory risks, and recommends avoidance measures, mitigation measures, and best management practices to minimize environmental impacts and regulatory risk.
Applies and interprets federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, permits, agreements, authorizations, and SFPUC policies, including the Raker Act.
Prepares or coordinates permit applications, right-of-way and special use authorization requests, and related submissions to local, state, and federal agencies.
Obtains authorizations under CWA

401/404, NPDES
402, Fish & Game Code

1602/1610, ESA/CESA, NHPA
106, ARPA, FLPMA, Raker Act, Wilderness Act, Wild & Scenic Rivers Act, and related federal/state authorities. Prepares, reviews, and coordinates CEQA, NEPA, NHPA, FLPMA, and related environmental review and compliance documentation.
Prepares and manages technical studies and reports concerning environmental, biological, cultural, land, and other natural resource matters.
Critically reviews and evaluates consultant work associated with planning, permitting, environmental review, technical studies, and compliance monitoring, and develops scopes of work and supports consultant contract administration, including schedules, budgets, deliverables, and fieldwork coordination.
Coordinates interdisciplinary review of project proposals, technical studies, and environmental documentation; performs environmental review of third-party applications for use of SFPUC lands.
Identifies environmental and regulatory risks, evaluates available information, and develops practical recommendations when requirements or project conditions are uncertain.
Represents SFPUC interests during interagency consultations, stakeholder meetings, public meetings, and field visits, and collaborates with multidisciplinary staff, consultants, regulatory personnel, Tribal representatives, and other parties.
Exercise sound and objective judgment, including when information is incomplete, requirements are uncertain, or competing priorities must be reconciled.
Manages competing priorities and communicates emerging issues, schedule risks, and recommended actions to project managers and supervisors.
Communicate complex legal, technical, and procedural information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university AND four (4) years (8000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

OR

Master's degree from an accredited college or university in city/regional/urban planning, environmental studies, architecture, law, earth sciences, geography, economics, landscape architecture, civil engineering, urban studies or public administration AND two (2) years (4000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

AND

License: Possession of a current valid California Driver’s License.

Note:
One (1) year of full-time employment is considered equivalent to two thousand (2,000) hours. Any overtime hours that you work above forty (40) hours per week are not included in the calculation to determine full-time employment.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

Desirable Qualifications:
The stated desirable qualifications may be considered at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring:

Experience interpreting or working with federal land management and permitting instruments including rights-of-way, special use authorizations, permits, easements, agreements, maps, land records, or historical authorizations.
Experience applying local, state, and federal environmental laws, regulations, and environmental review processes.
Experience with cultural resources identification, preservation, protection, consultation, and management practices.
Experience conducting environmental review and permitting for utility, infrastructure, operations, maintenance, or capital improvement activities.
Experience using GIS, databases, document management systems, or other tools to organize and analyze environmental, geographic, or regulatory information.
Experience developing scopes of work and supporting consultant contract administration, schedules, budgets, and multidisciplinary technical teams.
Experience coordinating with regulatory agencies, land management agencies, Tribal representatives, project managers, operations staff, consultants, attorneys, or other parties with differing responsibilities and perspectives.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the minimum qualifications as listed in the job ad. Please review our articles on Employment Application and Minimum Qualifications and Verification of Experience and/or Education for considerations taken when reviewing applications.

Verification:
Applicants may be required to submit verification of qualifying education and experience at any point during the recruitment and selection process. If education verification is required, information on how to verify education requirements, including verifying foreign education credits or degree equivalency, can be found at How to Verify Education Requirements

Note:
Falsifying one’s education, training, or work experience or attempted deception on the application may result in disqualification for this and future job opportunities with the City and County of San Francisco.

All work experience, education, training and other information substantiating how you meet the minimum qualifications must be included on your application by the filing deadline. Information submitted after the filing deadline will not be considered in determining whether you meet the minimum qualifications.

Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of a completed City and County of San Francisco application.

Applications completed improperly may be cause for ineligibility, disqualification or may lead to lower scores.

jobs.description:
Lead engineering, design, and permitting for environmental projects across the USVI and mainland U.S. You'll evaluate site assessment data, engineer solutions, and oversee projects from design through construction and operation. Relocation assistance available for qualified candidates.

Job Summary

As a Senior Environmental Engineer, you'll be a technical leader on our team, responsible for engineering quality from initial assessment through closeout. You'll work independently, guide project teams and subcontractors, and represent Tysam Tech with clients and regulatory agencies. This role suits an engineer who wants to solve the environmental challenges specific to island infrastructure and play a direct part in growing our practice.

The position is based in St. Croix or St. Thomas, USVI with a regular on-site presence at client facilities, and supports projects throughout the US Virgin Islands and the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Evaluate site assessment data and recommend corrective action.
Lead field investigations, including drilling, monitoring well installation, and sampling of soil, air, surface water, and groundwater.
Develop remediation designs, plans, specifications, and engineering calculations.
Prepare permit applications, regulatory submittals, and responses to agency comments.
Manage construction quality assurance to confirm work meets design documents.
Monitor the performance of completed systems and recommend operational improvements.
Support client compliance programs, including air permits, TPDES, SPCC, CZM, and EPCRA.
Perform quality control review of all reports, designs, calculations, and data before submission.
Direct contractors, subcontractors, and CAD drafters, and coordinate with clients on project deliverables.
Mentor and develop junior engineers and specialists.

Qualifications

B.S. in Environmental Engineering or similar engineering degree
5+ years of environmental engineering experience; consulting experience preferred
PE license, or EIT with the ability to obtain a PE within 12 months of hire
Stormwater design and water/wastewater plant design experience preferred
Valid driver's License with a driving record in good standing required
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship

Travel

Up to 20%

Compensation & Benefits

Salary commensurate with experience. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k), paid holidays, vacation, and an annual incentive program.

About Tysam Tech, LLC

Tysam Tech provides engineering and environmental services built for the unique needs of island-based businesses, government agencies, and industrial facilities. Founded in St. Croix, we support federal, territorial, and private clients across the Caribbean and mainland U.S. For more information, visit www.tysamtech.com.

Job Description

About bp / bpx

At bp, we’re reimagining energy for people and our planet. Within Production & Operations, bpx energy plays a critical role in delivering reliable energy while advancing our low carbon ambitions and reducing emissions across our operations.

Role Synopsis

The Environmental Engineer – Low Carbon is the subject matter expert in supporting bpx’s methane and carbon initiatives through emissions forecasting and accounting of emission projects, certification program coordination, and development of clear, data driven narratives. This role contributes to improving data quality and reporting transparency, and assists in air engineer job duties such as preparation of emission inventories and understanding sophisticated air regulations.

Key Responsibilities

Leading greenhouse gas forecasting by applying strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and sound judgment to recurring planning and reporting cycles.
Coordinating methane certification and assurance activities by organizing evidence, preparing for audits, tracking actions, and collaborating with internal teams and external reviewers.
Creating clear, compelling narratives and recommendations that explain methane management and emissions performance.
Determining insights by capturing inputs, performing quality checks, analyzing trends and variances, and maintaining clear documentation.
Partnering across environmental, engineering, operations, and digital teams to define data needs, resolve issues, and translate business requirements into practical, scalable solutions.
Simplify workflows, strengthen data governance, standardize processes, and identify opportunities to reduce manual effort and continuously improve.
Multi-functional and providing support in traditional environmental areas (e.g., air quality compliance, reporting) as business needs require.

Essential Education & Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or related technical field.
8 or more years of environmental, sustainability, or engineering roles with an emphasis on air quality in the oil and gas industry.
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to translate technical information into clear narratives.
Statistical and analytical thinking: Ability to evaluate datasets, perform basic statistical analysis, and identify trends, anomalies, and patterns in emissions or operational data.
Pattern recognition & problem solving: Ability to connect data insights to operational drivers and support development of actionable improvements.
Digital and data collaboration: Ability to work optimally with IT, data, or digital teams to define data needs, troubleshoot issues, and enable delivery of accurate and timely outputs to the business.
Strategic awareness: Interest in understanding how current data, tools, and processes support broader methane and carbon reduction goals, with the ability to contribute to discussions on future-state improvements.
Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill technical information into clear, stakeholder messaging.

Preferred Experience

Exposure to greenhouse gas inventories, emissions data, or sustainability reporting.
Curiosity about methane management, carbon reduction, or energy transition initiatives.

Why Join Us

You’ll be part of a team driving meaningful progress toward methane reduction and lower carbon energy systems—while gaining exposure to both low carbon strategy and traditional environmental engineering disciplines within a collaborative and fast paced environment.

Salary And Benefits

We offer a reward and wellbeing package to enable your work to fit with your life. These can include, but not limited to, access to health, vision and dental insurance, flexible working schedule, paid time off policy, discretionary annual bonus program, long-term incentive program, and a generous 401K matching program. How much do pay (base)? $130,000 - $160,000

Note that the pay range listed for this position is a good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible base compensation at the time of posting.

Travel Requirement

new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.

Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

Job Description

Eurofins Environment Testing in Little Rock, AR is seeking a Sample Receiving Technician to join our team. Our laboratory specializes in environmental testing. Providing analytical data and support to a diverse range of clients.

The Sample Receiving Technician is responsible for logging and tracking the receipt and shipment of samples into and out of the laboratory, verifying sample receipt, and supporting accurate and timely documentation. This role assists with preparing bottle kits for client delivery, sample login, labeling, routing, prioritization, and storage in accordance with Chain of Custody requirements and documented procedures. The Sample Receiving Technician may also support sample pick-up and delivery, customer service, courier duties, and the proper disposal of samples and waste in accordance with applicable procedures.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Receive and unload incoming samples or consignments in accordance with SOP; verify receipt against the Chain of Custody (COC), match samples to the corresponding quote, and document discrepancies daily. Review COCs for accuracy, completeness, and correctness, and seek resolution when needed.
Log samples into the laboratory information management system daily and assign job numbers for tracking purposes; distribute associated paperwork to Project Managers.
Label samples with assigned job numbers and deliver them to the appropriate laboratories for analysis each day.
Prepare bottle kits daily for shipment to clients for sample collection and return analysis, following established procedures, including EPA and DOT requirements.
Ship samples to other laboratories in accordance with DOT regulations when testing is not performed at the local facility.
Dispose of spent samples, waste, and other potentially hazardous materials in accordance with established procedures.
Clean and organize the department daily to maintain a safe, orderly work environment.
Maintain and promote safety by conducting all operations in a safe and environmentally compliant manner.
Stock supplies and assist with inventory management to ensure appropriate quantities of materials are available to perform assigned tasks.
Perform sample splitting and composites as requested.
Perform courier duties as needed to support laboratory and client requirements.
Comply with all driver procedures, certification requirements, and company driver policies.
Organize walk-in coolers to support sample storage and retrieval.
Ship empty coolers back to clients and other Eurofins laboratories; log all outgoing coolers to maintain a detailed cooler inventory.
Conduct all client interactions in a professional and courteous manner.
Perform other duties as assigned by local management.

Qualifications

High school diploma or GED required.
Valid state-issued driver’s license to operate company vehicles.
Basic computer skills include; ability to accurately input data into LIMS systems and ability to manage multiple emails.
Must be able to lift 55 lbs routinely and safely and must be able to work standing for most of the day
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English

Additional Information

This is a full time position Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. Some weekend work and overtime may be required.

Pay Rate Range for this position is $17 -$21 / hour (DOE).

Candidates within a commutable distance to Little Rock, AR are encouraged to apply.

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com

We support your development!
Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us!
At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Natural Resources and Lands Management Division:

The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on SFPUC lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations.

About the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section of NRLM:

The Moccasin Planning and Compliance (MPC) team is responsible for environmental review and permitting for the eastern division of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System and Hetch Hetchy Water and Power (HHWP), an operating division operating water, wastewater, and power infrastructure across the Sierra Nevada to the Bay Area.

Working Relationships:

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams.

The position requires effective communication, sound judgment, professionalism, and the ability to develop productive working relationships with individuals who may have different technical expertise, responsibilities, priorities, or perspectives.

Role Location:

There is currently one position available with the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division of the Water Enterprise. The position is located in Moccasin, California and the reporting location is in Moccasin, CA
(located 140 miles east of the San Francisco Bay Area
, requiring a 5-hour round trip commute from the San Francisco Bay Area, by car in fair weather).

Working Location:

The nature of the work may require working in remote field settings, including watersheds, streams, rivers, reservoirs, and federal lands. Duties may require driving or hiking to remote locations using unimproved dirt or mountain roads and working outdoors in inclement weather.

Job Description

Role Description:

The Environmental Planner performs complex environmental planning, permitting, compliance, and lands management work supporting operational and Capital Improvement Program activities of the SFPUC Water Enterprise, including CEQA/NEPA environmental review, Chapter 31 implementation, resource-agency permitting, environmental construction compliance, professional-services administration, federal-land coordination, natural and cultural resources management, Tribal engagement, and strategic program development.

This position reports to the Senior Environmental Planner of the Moccasin Planning and Compliance Section and may supervise the work of professional services consultants and junior planning staff. This is an external-facing position that works closely with federal and state agency staff, City attorneys, Tribal representatives, and SFPUC multidisciplinary teams. The incumbent develops project descriptions; evaluates environmental impacts and mitigation measures; prepares, manages, and reviews technical studies and regulatory documentation; supports professional services contract administration; coordinates multidisciplinary project teams; and provides technical guidance regarding environmental review, permitting, and regulatory compliance.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Analyzes proposed project activities to determine environmental review, documentation, consultation, and permitting requirements, identifies environmental and regulatory risks, and recommends avoidance measures, mitigation measures, and best management practices to minimize environmental impacts and regulatory risk.
Applies and interprets federal, state, and local laws, regulations, ordinances, permits, agreements, authorizations, and SFPUC policies, including the Raker Act.
Prepares or coordinates permit applications, right-of-way and special use authorization requests, and related submissions to local, state, and federal agencies.
Obtains authorizations under CWA

401/404, NPDES
402, Fish & Game Code

1602/1610, ESA/CESA, NHPA
106, ARPA, FLPMA, Raker Act, Wilderness Act, Wild & Scenic Rivers Act, and related federal/state authorities. Prepares, reviews, and coordinates CEQA, NEPA, NHPA, FLPMA, and related environmental review and compliance documentation.
Prepares and manages technical studies and reports concerning environmental, biological, cultural, land, and other natural resource matters.
Critically reviews and evaluates consultant work associated with planning, permitting, environmental review, technical studies, and compliance monitoring, and develops scopes of work and supports consultant contract administration, including schedules, budgets, deliverables, and fieldwork coordination.
Coordinates interdisciplinary review of project proposals, technical studies, and environmental documentation; performs environmental review of third-party applications for use of SFPUC lands.
Identifies environmental and regulatory risks, evaluates available information, and develops practical recommendations when requirements or project conditions are uncertain.
Represents SFPUC interests during interagency consultations, stakeholder meetings, public meetings, and field visits, and collaborates with multidisciplinary staff, consultants, regulatory personnel, Tribal representatives, and other parties.
Exercise sound and objective judgment, including when information is incomplete, requirements are uncertain, or competing priorities must be reconciled.
Manages competing priorities and communicates emerging issues, schedule risks, and recommended actions to project managers and supervisors.
Communicate complex legal, technical, and procedural information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university AND four (4) years (8000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

OR

Master's degree from an accredited college or university in city/regional/urban planning, environmental studies, architecture, law, earth sciences, geography, economics, landscape architecture, civil engineering, urban studies or public administration AND two (2) years (4000 hours) of verifiable full-time equivalent experience either:
performing environmental review functions OR
in a city/regional/urban planning environment preparing documents for entities such as California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), California Department of Fish and Game, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

AND

License: Possession of a current valid California Driver’s License.

Note:
One (1) year of full-time employment is considered equivalent to two thousand (2,000) hours. Any overtime hours that you work above forty (40) hours per week are not included in the calculation to determine full-time employment.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

Desirable Qualifications:
The stated desirable qualifications may be considered at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring:

Experience interpreting or working with federal land management and permitting instruments including rights-of-way, special use authorizations, permits, easements, agreements, maps, land records, or historical authorizations.
Experience applying local, state, and federal environmental laws, regulations, and environmental review processes.
Experience with cultural resources identification, preservation, protection, consultation, and management practices.
Experience conducting environmental review and permitting for utility, infrastructure, operations, maintenance, or capital improvement activities.
Experience using GIS, databases, document management systems, or other tools to organize and analyze environmental, geographic, or regulatory information.
Experience developing scopes of work and supporting consultant contract administration, schedules, budgets, and multidisciplinary technical teams.
Experience coordinating with regulatory agencies, land management agencies, Tribal representatives, project managers, operations staff, consultants, attorneys, or other parties with differing responsibilities and perspectives.

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted.

Every application is reviewed to ensure that you meet the minimum qualifications as listed in the job ad. Please review our articles on Employment Application and Minimum Qualifications and Verification of Experience and/or Education for considerations taken when reviewing applications.
